sections.name: WebGLInitializationError
sections.title: Special error for 3D startup failure
sections.what: Defines an error type used only when the 3D renderer cannot start. It keeps the original cause and uses a fixed message saying the browser could not initialize the 3D renderer.
sections.why: Lets the boundary catch only this failure, so unrelated bugs still show up as bugs.
sections.watch_out: Only renderer creation should throw this error. Any other code that throws it will show the WebGL fallback for the wrong reason.

summary: Defines a special error that means the browser could not start the 3D renderer.
purpose: Lets the error boundary recognize one specific failure and show the 3D fallback, while every other error still surfaces normally.
why: The comment says only renderer construction failures should show the compatibility fallback, which keeps real bugs from being hidden behind the wrong message.
how: When the renderer cannot be created, the code wraps the original cause in this error. The error boundary checks for this type and shows the fallback when it matches.
inputs: The original error that the browser threw, passed in as the cause.
outputs: An error object with a fixed message and the name WebGLInitializationError, carrying the original cause.
risks: If other code throws this error, the fallback will show for a problem that is not about WebGL. Missing the cause would make the original reason harder to find.
debug: If the fallback appears unexpectedly, check where this error was thrown. If a real WebGL failure shows a general error instead, check that the renderer creation step wraps its error with this type.
